title: The Delhi Excise Policy Case
dek: A liquor licensing policy was withdrawn amid allegations that it was designed to funnel kickbacks to a group of favoured liquor businesses. Years of arrests and headlines later, a trial court discharged every accused, finding no evidence the CBI's case could actually support.

heroStat.label: accused discharged by the trial court, February 2026

promise.quote: Delhi's new excise policy will end the cartelisation of liquor licences, increase government revenue, and be implemented transparently.
promise.madeBy: Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, under the Aam Aadmi Party
promise.role: State government implementing a new liquor retail licensing regime
promise.context: Delhi's Excise Policy 2021-22 restructured liquor retail licensing; it was withdrawn in mid-2022 after allegations that its design favoured a group of private liquor businesses referred to in the case as the 'South Group,' in exchange for kickbacks.

target.description: A licensing policy designed and implemented without favouritism toward specific private parties, and without kickbacks influencing its terms.
target.standard: Standard public procurement and policy-making norms requiring transparent, non-discriminatory treatment of private parties.

reality.description: The CBI and ED alleged the policy was designed to benefit the 'South Group' in exchange for illegal gratification quantified at roughly ₹90–100 crore, and arrested Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia in February 2023 and Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal in March 2024, among others. On 27 February 2026, a trial court discharged Kejriwal, Sisodia, and 21 others, finding the CBI had failed to substantiate its allegations with credible evidence and that no prima facie case of criminal conspiracy existed. The CBI has filed a revision petition in the Delhi High Court challenging the discharge, which was pending as of the most recent reporting reviewed.

gap.metricLabel: Accused named in the case vs. accused discharged by the trial court
gap.note: Every named accused in this case was discharged by the trial court in February 2026 — a stronger outcome for the accused than an acquittal after trial, since it means the court found insufficient evidence even to proceed to trial. The CBI's challenge to this finding was pending at the time of publication.

legalStatus.summary: As of publication, every person named in this case has been discharged by the trial court, which found the prosecution's evidence insufficient even to proceed to trial. That finding is being challenged by the CBI and is not yet final.

keyIndividuals.name: Arvind Kejriwal
keyIndividuals.outcome: Arrested March 2024; discharged by the trial court, February 2026, which found no prima facie evidence against him. CBI revision petition against the discharge pending.

keyIndividuals.name: Manish Sisodia
keyIndividuals.role: then Deputy Chief Minister of Delhi
keyIndividuals.outcome: Arrested February 2023; granted bail August 2024 after roughly 17 months in custody; discharged by the trial court, February 2026. CBI revision petition pending.

verdict.summary: This case's most important fact, and one easy to miss in year-old headlines, is its most recent development: a trial court did not merely acquit the accused after a trial — it discharged all 23 of them, finding the CBI's evidence insufficient to even proceed, and explicitly rebuked the agency's case. That finding is under challenge and not final, but as of publication it is the actual legal status, and this site reports it as such rather than defaulting to the more dramatic, better-known arrest narrative.
verdict.reasoning: The discharge order and the CBI's pending challenge to it are both documented in contemporaneous legal reporting. Confidence is not higher only because the matter remains open pending the High Court's ruling on the CBI's revision petition, and this investigation has not reviewed the discharge order's full text directly.

incomplete: The Delhi High Court had not ruled on the CBI's revision petition against the discharge as of this entry's publication.
The ED's separate money-laundering case, and its current status relative to the CBI matter's discharge, has not been fully detailed here.
This investigation has not reviewed the trial court's discharge order directly, relying instead on legal-affairs reporting of its content.
